note: Gregor et al. (2018) and subsequent cohort studies document recurrent dysmorphic features in FBXO11-related disorder, making the hypothesis plausible and worth in-depth evaluation.

evidence.text: Gregor et al. (2018) identified 20 individuals with de novo variants in FBXO11 presenting with developmental delay, behavioral anomalies, and variable dysmorphisms.

source.title: De novo variants in the F-box protein FBXO11 in 20 individuals with a variable neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: displaying minor and nonspecific dysmorphic features

numbers.metric: cleft lip or palate or bifid uvula

evidence.text: In a study assessing 21 individuals with FBXO11 pathogenic variants, facial dysmorphism was one of the most prevalent manifestations, observed in 67% of patients.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Mild intellectual disability (86%), facial dysmorphism (67%), hypotonia (62%), and behavioural dysregulation (62%) were the most prevalent features.
